title: Eventual rank unimodality conjecture
statement:
Let $N(m,n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ with rank $m$. **Eventual rank unimodality conjecture.** For $n\geq39$ and $0\leq m\leq n-3$, one has

$$
N(m,n)\geq N(m+1,n).
$$

By the symmetry $N(m,n)=N(-m,n)$, this gives unimodality of the rank distribution in the relevant range. The conjecture was proposed in earlier work and is proved in this paper by a Circle Method argument.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.12239

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2022). “Dyson's conjecture was proved by Atkin and Swinnerton-Dyer .”
source_name: Kathrin Bringmann, Siu Hang Man and Larry Rolen, “Unimodality of ranks and a proof of Stanton's conjecture”, arXiv:2209.12239 (2022).
